```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(htmltools)
library(DT)
library(leaflet)

# Logo paths come from _quarto.yml — change once, applies everywhere.
logo_tlu     <- file.path("..", course_meta("logo-tlu"))
logo_taltech <- file.path("..", course_meta("logo-taltech"))

logos_html <- function(height = "70px") {
  tags$div(
    style = "display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:60px;",
    tags$img(src = logo_tlu,     height = height),
    tags$img(src = logo_taltech, height = height)
  )
}

# Small fake bathing water dataset — embedded in slides for live demos
set.seed(42)
bw_sample <- tibble::tibble(
  country  = rep(c("EE", "LV", "LT", "FI", "SE"), each = 8),
  site     = c(
    "Pärnu rand", "Pirita rand", "Narva-Jõesuu", "Haapsalu",
    "Võrtsjärv", "Pühajärv", "Viljandi järv", "Ülemiste",
    "Jūrmala", "Liepāja", "Ventspils", "Saulkrasti",
    "Engure", "Rāzna", "Lubāns", "Burtnieks",
    "Palanga", "Klaipėda", "Neringa", "Šventoji",
    "Trakai", "Molėtai", "Druskininkai", "Kaunas",
    "Helsinki/Hietaranta", "Turku/Ruissalo", "Tampere/Kaukajärvi", "Oulu/Nallikari",
    "Lahti/Mukkulan", "Jyväskylä/Äijälänranta", "Rovaniemi/Ounasranta", "Espoo/Svinö",
    "Stockholm/Långholmen", "Göteborg/Askimsbadet", "Malmö/Ribersborg",
    "Uppsala/Flottsund", "Västerås/Lögarängsbadet", "Örebro/Oset",
    "Linköping/Tinnerö", "Helsingborg/Råå"
  ),
  type     = c(
    "coastal","coastal","coastal","coastal","inland","inland","inland","inland",
    "coastal","coastal","coastal","coastal","inland","inland","inland","inland",
    "coastal","coastal","coastal","coastal","inland","inland","inland","inland",

# Colour palette reused in both DT and map
quality_colours <- c(
  "Excellent" = "#2196F3",
  "Good"      = "#4CAF50",
  "Sufficient"= "#FF9800",
  "Poor"      = "#F44336"
)

# Live weather at render time
resp <- request("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast") |>
  req_url_query(
    latitude  = 58.38, longitude = 26.72,
    current   = "temperature_2m,wind_speed_10m",
    timezone  = "Europe/Tallinn"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

temp     <- resp$current$temperature_2m
wind     <- resp$current$wind_speed_10m
rendered <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
```

## General information

| Field | Proposed specification |
|---|---|
| Course code | MLB7052.LT |
| Course title | Kaasaegsed meetodid molekulaarses ökoloogias / Modern Molecular Methods in Ecology |
| Semester | 2026/2027 autumn |
| Language | Estonian teaching; English reading and software documentation |
| Lecturer | Peeter Laas |
| Assessment | Graded: A, B, C, D, E, F |
| Intended audience | Advanced undergraduate and master's students in molecular ecology, biology, biotechnology, and related fields |

::: {style="margin-top:1em; font-size:0.78em; color:#777;"}
Empty folder → 35 slides → shinyapps.io · `r temp`°C in Tartu at render time
:::

---

##  Course purpose

::: {.incremental}
1. understand the molecular principles behind DNA, RNA, proteins, genomes, gene expression, and molecular phenotypes;
2. understand the strengths, weaknesses, and appropriate uses of major molecular methods in ecology and evolutionary biology;
3. develop practical competence in sample design, nucleic-acid extraction, quantification, PCR, electrophoresis, sequencing, and basic computational analysis;
4. learn to connect molecular observations with ecological interactions, population structure, phylogeny, and environmental change;
5. develop reproducible habits for controls, contamination prevention, metadata, quality assessment, and scientific reporting;
6. design an end-to-end molecular study and defend the limitations of the proposed inference.
:::

---

## The main aim

The course develops a working understanding of molecular biology and its use in ecological and evolutionary research. Students move from the molecular basis of information to a defensible study design:

**biological question -> sample -> molecule -> assay -> sequence or measurement -> computation -> inference**

::: {.notes}
The goal isn't to replace thinking — it's to reduce friction. You still need to understand the code.
:::

---

# The course

---

## Course content {.scrollable}

::: {.dropdown-table}

<details>
<summary><strong>Block I</strong> — Foundations and measurement</summary>

- evolution, scientific reasoning, and molecular biology as a way of knowing;
- chemical properties of DNA, RNA, proteins, buffers, enzymes, and molecular interactions;
- information flow, replication, mutation, repair, recombination, transcription, translation, and regulation;
- sample representativeness, preservation, extraction, quantification, inhibition, and contamination.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Block II</strong> — The molecular toolkit</summary>

- electrophoresis, restriction analysis, Southern blotting, PCR, qPCR, ddPCR, Sanger sequencing, probes, FISH, fluorescence, and flow cytometry;
- molecular markers, barcoding, metabarcoding, allozymes, RFLP, microsatellites, and SNPs;
- Illumina, PacBio, Oxford Nanopore, library preparation, read quality, assembly, annotation, and data management.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Block III</strong> — Genomes and molecular phenotypes</summary>

- comparative genomics, assembly, annotation, and public sequence databases;
- transcriptomics, non-coding RNA, stage- and condition-specific regulation, epigenetics, and functional genomics;
- proteomics, quantitative proteomics, protein interactions, post-translational modification, and molecular phenotypes;
- the cell biology behind the traits we measure: life-cycle stages, secretion, transport, and cellular responses to the environment.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Block IV</strong> — Ecology, evolution, and application</summary>

- phylogeny, phylogeography, population genetics, coalescence, and community-level inference;
- species interactions, symbiosis, host-associated microbiota, and environmental monitoring;
- CRISPR, LAMP, microfluidics, lab-on-chip, biosensing, and field-deployable diagnostics;

</details>

:::

## Live data in slides — weather example

Slides fetch real data at **render time**. No manual updates ever.

```{r}
#| label: weather-demo
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(httr2)

resp <- request("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast") |>
  req_url_query(
    latitude  = 58.38,   # Tartu
    longitude = 26.72,
    current   = "temperature_2m,wind_speed_10m",
    timezone  = "Europe/Tallinn"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

temp <- resp$current$temperature_2m
wind <- resp$current$wind_speed_10m
```

Then in slide text:

```markdown
Temperature in Tartu right now: **`{r} temp`°C**, wind `{r} wind` km/h
```

**This title slide already does this** — look at the subtitle line.

## Demo — downloadable table {.scrollable}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
bw_sample |>
  mutate(quality = factor(quality,
           levels = c("Excellent","Good","Sufficient","Poor"))) |>
  datatable(
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options    = list(
      dom        = "Bfrtip",
      buttons    = list(
        list(extend = "csv",   text = "Download CSV"),
        list(extend = "excel", text = "Download Excel")
      ),
      pageLength = 8,
      scrollY    = "340px",
      scrollCollapse = TRUE
    ),
    filter   = "top",
    rownames = FALSE,
    colnames = c("Country","Site","Type","Quality","Season","Lon","Lat")
  ) |>
  formatStyle(
    "quality",
    backgroundColor = styleEqual(
      names(quality_colours), unname(quality_colours)
    ),
    color = "white", fontWeight = "bold"
  )
```

---

## Demo — interactive map

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
pal <- colorFactor(palette = unname(quality_colours),
                   levels  = names(quality_colours))

leaflet(bw_sample) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.DarkMatter) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng         = ~lon,
    lat         = ~lat,
    color       = ~pal(quality),
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    radius      = 9,
    stroke      = FALSE,
    popup       = ~paste0(
      "<b>", site, "</b><br>",
      country, " &middot; ", type, "<br>",
      "<b style='color:", quality_colours[quality], "'>",
      quality, "</b> &middot; ", season
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~quality,
            title = "Quality", opacity = 0.9)
```

## Exercise 1 — Explore the data (15 min)

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

bw <- read_csv("bw_assessment_eea_datahub_1990_2024_data.csv",
               show_col_types = FALSE)

glimpse(bw)
count(bw, countryCode, sort = TRUE)
count(bw, quality)
```

Answer from the output, not from memory:

- how many bathing waters does Estonia report, and over which years?
- which quality categories exist, and how are they distributed?
- which columns would you need to put a site on a map?

---

## Exercise 2 — Filter and summarise (15 min)

```r
bw_ee <- bw |>
  filter(countryCode == "EE", season == 2024)

bw_ee |>
  count(quality) |>
  mutate(share = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

Then plot how the ratings have moved over time:

```r
library(ggplot2)

bw |>
  filter(countryCode == "EE") |>
  count(season, quality) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, n, fill = quality)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "share of sites", fill = NULL)
```

---

## Exercise 3 — A searchable, downloadable table (15 min)

A large data frame can be made browsable and downloadable:

```r
library(DT)

bw_ee |>
  select(bathingWaterName, bathingWaterType,
         lon, lat, quality, season) |>
  datatable(
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options = list(
      dom       = "Bfrtip",
      buttons   = c("csv", "excel"),
      pageLength = 15
    ),
    filter    = "top",      # per-column filter boxes
    rownames  = FALSE
  )
```

This renders as an interactive HTML table with search, sort, and download — it
works in any self-contained `.html` and in a Shiny app.

---

## Exercise 4 — Build the report (25 min)

Put the three previous steps into one `report.qmd`:

```yaml
---
title: "Estonian bathing waters, 1990-2024"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---
```

1. read the data;
2. filter to Estonia;
3. show the searchable table;
4. plot the quality trend as a stacked bar chart;
5. `quarto render report.qmd`.

The output is a single HTML file you can email, and the `.qmd` beside it says
exactly how every number in it was produced.

---

## Key takeaways

::: {.incremental}
- **`_quarto.yml`** = set your identity and style once, reuse forever
- **Live data at render time** — slides and reports that never go stale
- **`DT`** turns a 600,000-row table into something searchable and downloadable
- **`leaflet`** puts sampling sites on a map in a dozen lines
- **Self-contained HTML** travels as one file — no folder of assets to lose
- **Commit first** — you cannot break what is already in git
:::
